route: brand-hosted review platform display APIs (Bazaarvoice, PowerReviews, Yotpo) - see brand-widget-routes-2026-10-15.json
why_this_file: A route reaching one member of a peer group cannot support peer-relative tone, which is the project's second specification (references/signal.md, S2). Coverage is therefore a per-group property, not a per-company one, and has to be written down per group or the S2 claim is unfalsifiable.
reached_means: a display API serves this member's reviews, with >= 2 years of dated text AND enough text-bearing reviews to clear the 30-per-quarter floor over a usable run of quarters AND a newest review recent enough to extend

summary.the_honest_shape: The route is excellent where it reaches and reaches four of seven declared groups' public members. Coverage splits on CHANNEL, not on company size: brands that sell direct from their own storefront run a review platform, and brands that sell through grocery, retail floors or carriers do not. Traeger, YETI, Premier Protein, Quest, Atkins, Olaplex and Turtle Beach are all DTC web storefronts. Celsius and Monster are grocery - and Red Bull, also grocery, is the exception that shows it is a choice rather than a law. That is the same DTC selection bias already recorded for the 10x Amazon asymmetry rule, arriving independently through a second sensor, which makes it a property of the companies rather than of either instrument.
summary.the_asymmetry_that_should_worry_the_proj: Of the five groups with a reachable member, the PRIVATE control is reachable in all five and the PUBLIC member in only four - and in wireless-speakers and energy-drinks the control is reachable while the company under test is not. The sensor sees category controls more reliably than it sees the companies whose revenue the project wants to predict. Private peers are over-represented because private consumer brands are disproportionately DTC, which is the same reason they looked healthiest under the 10x rule.
